result:
B1: PASS
Why: The synopsis says the plan aimed "to bring the `writing-skills` skill into line with the Claude Code guide and close three backlog items" because Claude Code-only advice "was mixed in with advice that holds on every runtime, and several claims had no support in the guide." It names the goal "to separate the two kinds of advice, correct those claims, and clear the stale citation," which matches the spec's distill, correct and restamp goals.

B2: PASS
Why: The order is the new `claude-code.md` file, then the trims and pointers in `discovery.md` and `SKILL.md` that depend on it, then the bookkeeping, then the micro-test evidence. No part comes before a part it needs. Two facts come from the diff and are not in the spec. First, "another's artifacts were extended": `build/cc_guide/conformance.toml` adds `skills/writing-skills/references/discovery.md` to the `artifacts` of `description-when-only`, which the spec said would stay unchanged. Second, "section hashes were added": `build/cc_guide/baseline.json` gains eight sha256 entries for `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md`.

B3: PASS
Why: The synopsis says the branch "removes every `STALE` lint line and closes three backlog items" and "opens five new items." That changes how the drift-lint workflow and the backlog behave for the whole project, not just the files touched.

B4: PASS
Contradicted: none
